name: Textarea
description: A multi-line field for longer free text, such as a message or a description. Use it when the answer may run past one line; for short values, use a Text input.

elements.name: Label
elements.description: Visible name linked with for; see Label

elements.name: Field
elements.description: The text box; its height, set with rows, hints at the expected length

elements.name: Character count
elements.description: Shows how many characters are left when there's a limit

elements.name: Resize handle
elements.description: Lets people drag the field taller; browsers add it by default

variants.caption: Rows — short and tall
variants.htmlOutline:
<label for="note">Note</label>
<textarea id="note" name="note" rows="2"></textarea>

<label for="msg">Message</label>
<textarea id="msg" name="msg" rows="8"></textarea>

variants.caption: Character count — characters left below the field
variants.htmlOutline: 500 characters left

variants.caption: Error — message above the field
variants.htmlOutline: Enter a message

usageNotes: Use a Textarea when the answer can be longer than a line. Use a Text input for short single-line values; Enter in a Textarea adds a line break instead of submitting the form.
Set rows to suit the expected length. If the height grows with the content, still allow vertical resizing so people can see more of what they wrote.

With a character limit, show how many characters remain and announce the count through a polite live region after typing pauses, not on every keystroke. Letting people go over and showing an error is kinder than maxlength, which silently cuts off pasted text.
Give it a visible <label> and link hints and errors with aria-describedby, as for a Text input.
The alias "Textbox" is the ARIA role a <textarea> already has (textbox with aria-multiline). The component keeps the HTML element's name.
